headline: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
deck: The Environment Agency has put parts of six counties under severe-drought status as the government prioritises public water supplies where unavoidable trade-offs arise.
body: England’s Environment Agency declared severe drought on 15 October in parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex, citing the potential impact on essential water resources. [E1][E4]
The agency said water supply was most at risk around Ardingly reservoir in West Sussex and Wimbleball reservoir in Somerset. [E2]

Water Minister Emma Hardy instructed the agency to prioritise protecting public water supplies in the severe-drought areas where environmental rules and water supplies face an unavoidable trade-off. [E3]
